hindi: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ के लिए माना कि $S_{n}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{n}{n^{2}+k}$ है। तब $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}n\left(S_{n}-1\right)$ बराबर है
solution: $S_{n}\to1$ only gives $0\cdot\infty$; write each term minus $\dfrac1n$: $\dfrac{n}{n^{2}+k}-\dfrac{1}{n}=-\dfrac{k}{n(n^{2}+k)}$
Both bounds are rational in $n$ with equal leading terms $\dfrac{n^{2}/2}{n^{2}}$, so both $\to\dfrac12$; hence $T_{n}\to\dfrac12$
solution_full: First, $\dfrac{n}{n^{2}+n}\le\dfrac{n}{n^{2}+k}\le\dfrac{n}{n^{2}+1}$, so $\dfrac{n^{2}}{n^{2}+n}\le S_{n}\le\dfrac{n^{2}}{n^{2}+1}$ and $S_{n}\to1$. This makes $n(S_{n}-1)$ a $0\cdot\infty$ form, so the first-order bound is not enough.

Subtract $\dfrac{1}{n}$ from each of the $n$ terms: $S_{n}-1=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\left(\dfrac{n}{n^{2}+k}-\dfrac{1}{n}\right)=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{n^{2}-(n^{2}+k)}{n(n^{2}+k)}=-\sum_{k=1}^{n}\dfrac{k}{n(n^{2}+k)}$.
For $1\le k\le n$, $n^{2}+1\le n^{2}+k\le n^{2}+n$, so $\dfrac{k}{n^{2}+n}\le\dfrac{k}{n^{2}+k}\le\dfrac{k}{n^{2}+1}$. Summing with $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}k=\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$:
The left bound equals $\dfrac{1}{2}$. The right bound is a rational function whose numerator and denominator both have leading term $n^{2}$, giving $\dfrac{n^{2}}{2n^{2}}\to\dfrac{1}{2}$.
By the sandwich theorem $T_{n}\to\dfrac{1}{2}$, so $\displaystyle\lim_{n\to\infty}n(S_{n}-1)=-\dfrac{1}{2}$. (Stopping at $S_{n}\to1$ suggests $0$; losing the sign gives $\dfrac{1}{2}$.)
originality_note: New: the first-order sandwich only gives S_n -> 1; the next-order term n(S_n - 1) is turned into a second sum that is itself squeezed (way 4, two orders). Closest known: lim sum n/(n^2+k) = 1 and lim sum k/(n^2+k) = 1/2. Different because: the question asks for the rate of convergence of the first sum, which needs the subtraction step before the standard sandwich.
blueprint_concepts: Limits at infinity; dominant term and rational function behaviour

concept_use.Sandwich Theorem: T_n is squeezed between n(n+1)/(2(n^2+n)) and n(n+1)/(2(n^2+1)), both tending to 1/2.
concept_use.Limits at infinity; dominant term and ra: The bounds are rational functions of n whose limits come from the leading n^2 terms; also used for S_n -> 1.
